articles.headline: Lauren Jackson on A'ja Wilson: 'There'd be battles, for sure'
articles.description: Australian basketball icon Lauren Jackson praises four-time WNBA MVP A'Ja Wilson, and believes the pair would've been a great matchup back in Jackson's prime.

articles.headline: A'ja Wilson, Kelsey Plum to miss the FIBA Women's World Cup
articles.description: Kelsey Plum and A'ja Wilson will miss the FIBA Women's World Cup for health reasons, with the Mercury announcing that Plum will miss the rest of the 2026 season. Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron will replace Plum and Wilson, USA Basketball announced Monday.

articles.headline: Angel Reese breaks WNBA record with 29th double-double
articles.description: Angel Reese had 15 points and 11 rebounds to break a WNBA record with her 29th double-double this season, and the Atlanta Dream defeated the league-leading Minnesota Lynx 89-81 on Sunday afternoon in their last game before the FIBA World Cup break.

article.story: LOS ANGELES -- — Nneka Ogwumike had 23 points and 12 rebounds, Rae Burrell scored 22 points, and the Los Angeles Sparks beat the Seattle Storm 90-74 on Sunday in their final game before the FIBA World Cup break. LA scored the first 13 points in an opening 18-2 run and Dearica Hamby's layup with 5:45 left in the first half capped an 11-0 spurt that gave the Sparks a 39-20 lead. Seattle shot 32% (12 of 38) from the field and 2 of 11 (18%) from behind the arc before going into halftime trailing by 19. The Storm were just as bad from 3-point range in the second half, finishing 4 of 22. Cameron Brink had 11 points on 3-of-15 shooting for the Sparks (15-25). Flau’jae Johnson scored 11 of her 19 points in the fourth quarter and Dominique Malonga had 17 points, on 8-of-21 shooting, and 15 rebounds for the Storm (8-32). Zia Cooke made 6 of 17 from the field for 14 points. Seattle is 1-18 against Western Conference teams this season, its only win coming at LA, 82-64, on July 6. The Storm's Jordan Horston fell awkwardly midway through the third quarter, limped to the locker room and did not return. Awa Fam and Natisha Hiedeman did not play for the Storm. Up next Sparks: Visit Dallas on Sept. 17. Storm: Host Las Vegas on Sept. 17. ------ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here
